key_insight: Adding Cr3C2-Ni80Cr20 to a CoCrFeMnNi0.8V HEA HVOF coating creates a dense, wear-resistant composite, but it also makes the coating more prone to chloride corrosion.
engineering_relevance: The coating is promising for surfaces needing high wear resistance and toughness, but designers must balance tribological gains against reduced electrochemical durability in salty environments.
method: HVOF-sprayed a 50 wt.% HEA / 50 wt.% Cr3C2-Ni80Cr20 powder blend onto steel.
Examined microstructure and phase evolution with microscopy and XRD.
Compared wear performance by ball-on-disc testing and corrosion behavior in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
evidence_signal: The composite coating was 450–500 μm thick, showed dense well-bonded multiphase microstructure, improved wear resistance, and had a corrosion current density of 10.53 × 10^-6 A/cm² in NaCl.
watch_item: The heterogeneous phase structure that improves wear can also promote micro-galvanic corrosion, so environmental exposure limits should be checked before deployment.
paper_title: Microstructure, Sliding Wear, and Electrochemical Corrosion of a High-Entropy Alloy–Cermet Composite Thermal Spray Coating
